sources.name: Building Height Attribute Getting Started Guide
sources.role: TOID format normalisation and join workflow contract
verified_facts: The guide requires users to compare TOID formats in translated Topography Layer data and BHA data before joining.
semantic_limits: String-normalisation success is not proof that the TOID version, building footprint or process date is compatible.

sources.name: Building Height Attribute Technical Specification
sources.role: absolute-relative height, selected-structure and TOID join contract
verified_facts: The specification covers absolute and relative values for buildings, tanks, industrial chimneys and glasshouses and requires joining by the building TOID.
semantic_limits: BHA requires the corresponding Topography feature and must not be used as an independent parcel or terrain source.

sources.name: Building Height Attribute Feature Type
sources.role: TOID, TOID version, process date, tile and height-field contract
verified_facts: The feature type includes OS_TOPO_TOID, OS_TOPO_TOID_VERSION, process date and tile reference; AbsHMax can include rooftop structures.
semantic_limits: A matching TOID without matching version and process-date checks can bind heights to the wrong building state.

sources.name: Building Height Attribute Downloads
verified_facts: The downloads page provides the BHA CSV header and related support resources.
semantic_limits: The header defines columns but is not the BHA data distribution and cannot prove target-row coverage.

sources.name: How to Read a Title Plan
sources.role: title number, register-plan pairing, red-edged extent and timestamp contract
verified_facts: A title plan supports the register description, uses Ordnance Survey mapping to indicate the registered extent and represents the state at its stated date and time.
semantic_limits: The visual extent must be read with the register and does not automatically identify an exact legal boundary.

sources.name: How to Read a Title Register
sources.role: A/B/C register sections, ownership, charges and timestamp contract
verified_facts: A title register is generally divided into property, proprietorship and charges sections and must usually be read with its title plan.
semantic_limits: A postal description or title number does not itself provide a machine-readable polygon or terrain measurement.

sources.name: Practice Guide 40 Overview
sources.role: plan-guide supplement scope and cross-document interpretation contract
verified_facts: The guide overview separates the basis of plans, plan preparation, boundaries, determined boundaries, title plans and related services into supplements.
semantic_limits: One supplement must not be used outside its scope to infer exact ownership, survey accuracy or current geometry.

sources.name: Practice Guide 40 Supplement 1 — Basis of Plans
sources.role: OS map basis, scale and topographic-feature representation contract
verified_facts: Ordnance Survey mapping records topographic features present at survey time and is not intended to represent property boundaries.
semantic_limits: A mapped fence, wall or line must not be assumed to be the legal boundary or an HMLR determined boundary.

sources.name: Practice Guide 40 Supplement 2 — Preparing Plans
sources.role: deed-plan quality, application-purpose and pre-registration-evidence contract
verified_facts: The guide states that title plans and registers cannot describe land more accurately than the pre-registration deeds and evidence allow.
semantic_limits: A well-drawn application plan does not upgrade underlying legal evidence or establish a surveyed terrain boundary.

sources.name: Practice Guide 40 Supplement 6 — Related Services
sources.role: index-map search, illustrative plan and electronic-extent-data service contract
verified_facts: The supplement describes searches of the index map, illustrative plans and Electronic Extent Data supplied as polygons.
semantic_limits: A service polygon is an index or management representation and must not be presented as a determined legal boundary.

sources.name: Finding Information Held by HM Land Registry
sources.role: standard result, official copy and legal-evidence role contract
verified_facts: Standard search results are generally suitable for checks, while an official copy may be required for legal purposes.
semantic_limits: A downloaded standard result and an official copy have different evidential roles; neither creates numeric elevation evidence.

sources.name: Electronic Extent Data Polygons
sources.role: bulk electronic extent and asset-management polygon contract
verified_facts: HM Land Registry supplies Electronic Extent Data polygons for asset, liability, planning and policy uses.
semantic_limits: Bulk extent polygons require title, currency and service-scope checks and must not be treated as surveyed exact boundaries.
